duAn.moTa: Each project has its own link. Anyone with the link can view; editing needs the project's edit code.
duAn.trong: No projects on this computer yet. Create a new one or open one by link.
duAn.maSuaMotLan: This is the only time the edit code is shown. Copy the edit link and keep it; without the code the project is view-only.
duAn.danLink: Paste a project link or code
duAn.linkSai: That is not a valid project link or code.
soan.khongCo: Project not found. Check the link.
soan.loiMang: Cannot reach the server. Try again later.
soan.chiXem: Read-only view. Editing needs the project's edit link.
soan.coNhap: There are unsaved changes from last time on this computer.
lo.dxfGiaiThich: Export the planning drawing from AutoCAD as DXF; each closed polygon on the plot layer becomes a plot. On land-use drawings with only hatched parcels, each hatch becomes a plot named after its land use.
lo.thayLo: Replace all current plots with the plots in this DXF?
lo.loi.ranh_khong_kin: The boundary layer only has open lines; closed polygons are needed.
lo.loi.lop_trong: The boundary layer has no lines.
lo.chuaCo: No plots yet. Import a planning DXF or add a rectangular plot in the left panel.
xep.chuaCoLo: No plots yet. Load a DXF or add a plot in step 1.
xep.loKhongXayO: This plot is not residential. Pick a commercial or social housing plot.
xep.thuVienGiaiThich: Towers that fit (fully inside the setback at some rotation) come first. Place puts the tower at the setback centre.
xep.chuaCoToa: No towers yet. Pick one from the library.
xep.keoGoiY: Drag a tower to move it; locked towers stay put.
lo.nguonCtNhom: This row covers {n} plots: population and units split by plot area.
nct.giaiThich: Reads the land-use indicator Excel, detects columns (land area, podium/tower coverage, basement/podium/tower floors, FAR, units, population) and matches each row to DXF plots by code or area. Check the area difference before applying.
nct.khongNhan: No indicator table found in this sheet (needs a header row with Area, Coverage, Floors…).
nct.dongThieuLo: Table rows with no DXF plot
nct.loChuaGhep: DXF plots with no table row
nct.ghiChuChia: A row matched to several plots: the area difference is for the group; population and units are split by plot area, coverage / FAR / floors are kept.
db.giaiThich: Paste a table copied from Excel (unit type, share %, units, unit area) or choose a file. Shares become the target mix; unit areas are compared when swapping unit types.
tang.chuaCoToa: No tower yet. Place one in step 2 · Place towers.
tang.mixGhiChu: The mix is only a guide: whole units cannot match the ratio exactly. Optimising only swaps to a type of the same width, depth and middle/corner position; units are never redrawn.
tang.suaNhieu: Edit many units (same type in this tower)
tang.phamVi: Typical floor applies to {n} apartment floors
tang.phanChungGhiChu: Common = corridor area {m} m² shared by unit gross area.
tang.uocTinh: Estimated from the axis because the tower has no corridor lines.
tang.chonMotCan: Click a unit on the plan to inspect and swap it.
tang.doiNhieu: Swap to a same-width type — applies to every unit of this type in the tower:
tang.doiMot: Swap to a same-width type — this unit only:
tang.khongCoMauDoi: No other type with the same width and depth.
tang.doiVeGoc: Back to the tower's original unit
duAn.xoaHoi: Delete option “{ten}”? This cannot be undone.
m3d.chuaCoDuLieu: No 3D data for this unit template.
m3d.goiY: Left drag: orbit · right drag or Shift: pan · wheel: zoom. Touch: 1 finger orbits, 2 fingers zoom / pan. Exported images are twice the view resolution. Storey height 3.3 m and podium floor 4 m are assumptions.
xcad.moTa: Typical floor plan of tower {t}, using the current unit templates.
xcad.scrMoTa: Put the file next to the library folder (cad/xref), open AutoCAD, run SCRIPT and pick it. The drawing references the library, so editing a unit template updates the plan.
xcad.dxfMoTa: Stand-alone file in mm: one BLOCK per unit template, one INSERT per position, plus the floor-area outline and corridors.
m3d.aiGiaiThich: Copy a description to paste into an AI render tool together with the exported image (White model style works best).
m3d.promptAI: Photorealistic architectural rendering of the residential high-rise project "{ten}" in Hanoi, Vietnam. Keep the exact massing, tower positions and camera angle of the reference image. Modern facades with glass and light stone, balconies with greenery, landscaped podium gardens, tree-lined streets, natural daylight around {gio}:00, soft shadows, realistic people and cars at street level, high detail, 4K.
gt.ct.matDoMax: Maximum building coverage (%) = building footprint / plot area. When the planning table separates podium and tower, this is the podium coverage. Taken from the approved planning-indicator table.
gt.ct.matDoThapMax: Maximum tower coverage (%). Leave empty if the planning table gives no separate tower value. Taken from the approved planning-indicator table.
gt.ct.hssddMax: Maximum floor-area ratio = total floor area including basements (excluding technical, fire-fighting, refuge and parking floor area) / plot area. Basis: QCVN 01:2021/BXD, 1.4.21.
gt.ct.tangCaoMax: Maximum number of storeys above ground, basements excluded. From 5 storeys at least 1 lift, from 10 storeys at least 2 (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.4.1). Taken from the approved planning-indicator table.
gt.ct.tangDe: Number of podium storeys per the planning table. Leave empty if not specified.
gt.ct.tangCanHo: Number of apartment storeys in the tower per the planning table. Leave empty if not specified.
gt.ct.tangHam: Number of basement levels per the planning table. Minimum clear height of a basement 2.0 m (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.2.10). Leave empty if not specified.
gt.ct.soCanMax: Number of apartments per the planning table. If empty, estimated from maximum population and persons per unit. Minimum lifts: 1 per 200 people or per 70 units (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.4.2).
gt.ct.danSoMax: Maximum population of the plot (people) per the planning. Used to estimate the unit count when the table gives none. Taken from the approved planning-indicator table.
gt.ct.nguoiMoiCan: Average persons per unit, used to convert population into an estimated unit count. No QCVN basis. Provisional value, awaiting the lead's decision.
gt.ct.choDoOtoMoiCan: Minimum car spaces per unit, used for the parking demand. A space is at least 5 m x 2.3 m, wheelchair space 3.5 m wide (QCVN 13:2018/BXD, 2.2.1.25). Total parking area including internal lanes at least 25 m² per 4 units and 20 m² per 100 m² of unit area (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.2.17.1). The default per-unit count is provisional, awaiting the lead's decision.
gt.ct.choXeMayMoiCan: Minimum motorbike spaces per unit. Motorbike/bicycle parking area at least 6 m² per unit (60% for social housing) (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.2.17.1). The default per-unit count is provisional, awaiting the lead's decision.
gt.ct.cayXanhMin: Minimum green-space share of the plot area (%). Taken from the approved planning-indicator table.
gt.lo.kyHieu: Plot code as in the planning drawing, shown on the drawing and in the plot list. Renaming does not change geometry.
gt.lo.chucNang: Plot function: commercial housing, social housing or other. Decides which tower library is offered and the land-use colour. Units under 45 m² are limited to 25% of all units in commercial housing (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.2.4.2).
gt.coCau.o: Share (%) of units of this type in the plot's target mix; the shares must total 100%. Minimum unit 25 m² (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.2.4.1); commercial housing: units under 45 m² at most 25% of all units (2.2.4.2). The default mix is provisional, awaiting the lead's decision. A business brief overrides it when imported.
gt.lo.dxf: Load the site DXF: export the planning drawing from AutoCAD; each closed polygon on the plot layer becomes a plot, or each hatch on a land-use drawing.
gt.lo.bangQH: Import the planning-indicator Excel and match each row with a plot (by code or area). Check the area-difference column before applying.
gt.lo.deBai: Import the business brief: wanted share and area per unit type. Shares become the plot's target mix; areas drive the colour dots when swapping units.
gt.lo.themTay: Add a rectangular plot by hand when there is no DXF. Enter width and length in metres, then press Add.
gt.lo.them: Add the rectangular plot next to the existing ones.
gt.lo.lopRanh: DXF layer holding the plot boundaries. Each closed polygon on it becomes a plot. "Hatch" = each filled land parcel becomes a plot.
gt.lo.lopChiGioi: DXF layer holding the building line (limit of the buildable area). Leave empty for no building line.
gt.lo.lopTem: DXF layer holding the plot code text; used to name plots and infer land use.
gt.lo.lopXungQuanh: DXF layer holding surrounding buildings, drawn as reference only and not counted in the indicators.
gt.lo.taoTuDxf: Create the plots from the DXF using the selected layers. Replaces all existing plots (asks first).
gt.lo.chonLo: Pick the high-rise housing plot to work on. Other parcels are only shown as background.
gt.nct.chonTep: Choose the Excel file with the planning-indicator table (.xlsx, .xls, .xlsm). Columns are detected from their headers.
gt.nct.sheet: Choose the sheet with the indicator table. Changing it re-reads and re-matches.
gt.nct.dongBang: Table row matched to this plot. Change it by hand if the automatic match is wrong; several plots may share a row, then population and unit count are split by plot area.
gt.db.dan: Paste a table copied from Excel: columns unit type, share %, count, area (m²), tab-separated. The result appears in the preview below.
gt.db.chonTep: Or choose the business brief Excel file; the first sheet with unit-type rows is picked automatically.
gt.db.sheet: Sheet of the brief Excel file to read.
gt.db.apCho: Where to apply the brief's mix and unit areas: only the selected plot, all plots of the same function, or all housing plots.
gt.muc.chiTieuQH: Planning indicators of the selected plot (coverage, FAR, height, population, parking, green). Enter by hand or import from the Excel table. QCVN clauses are given in each field.
gt.muc.coCauMucTieu: Target unit mix of the plot: % per unit type, total 100%. Source: business brief or manual entry. Compared with the actual mix of the towers in the right-hand panel.
gt.muc.sucChua: Theoretical capacity of the plot from the planning indicators: footprint, floor area, units, parking, green required.
gt.muc.chiTieuLo: Compares what the scheme achieves with the plot's planning targets. Red = exceeded, amber = warning, green = met.
gt.xep.toaTrenLo: Towers already placed on the plot. Click one to select and edit it.
gt.xep.thongSo: Parameters of the selected tower: storeys, rotation, podium offset and centre position. A locked tower cannot be edited.
gt.xep.dtLo: Areas on the plot: plot area, podium area, floor area counted in FAR, coverage and FAR of the scheme. FAR = total floor area / plot area (QCVN 01:2021/BXD, 1.4.21).
gt.xep.coCau: Actual unit mix of the plot per tower, against the target mix. Beyond the colour threshold it turns red.
gt.tang.toa: Towers in the scheme. Click one to view and edit its typical floor plan.
gt.tang.hienThi: Floor-plan display options: drawing style, unit labels, furniture, colour dots against the brief, multi-unit editing.
gt.tang.canTrongToa: Number of units of each type in the tower's typical floor against the plot's target mix. Beyond the threshold it turns red.
gt.tang.loaiCanTrongTang: Unit templates in use on the floor. Clear area per QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 1.4.13: measured inside walls, including balconies and loggias, excluding columns, load-bearing walls, shafts, outer walls and party walls. Common share is the corridor area split among the units.
gt.tang.canDangChon: The unit selected on the drawing: size, clear area (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 1.4.13) and replacement templates. Minimum unit 25 m² (2.2.4.1).
gt.xep.soTangDH: Number of repeated typical storeys above the podium. From 5 storeys at least 1 lift, from 10 storeys at least 2 (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.4.1). Minimum 1.
gt.xep.soTangDe: Number of podium storeys (retail, parking, amenities) under the tower. 0 if no podium. Compare with the plot's planning podium storeys.
gt.xep.goc: Rotation of the tower about its centre, in degrees. It can also be rotated on the drawing.
gt.xep.deOffset: How far the podium extends beyond the tower footprint (m). 0 = podium equals the tower footprint. The podium must stay inside the building line.
gt.xep.x: X coordinate of the tower centre on the plot (m), in drawing coordinates.
gt.xep.y: Y coordinate of the tower centre on the plot (m), in drawing coordinates.
gt.xep.nhanBan: Duplicate the tower and place the copy beside the original along the tower's width.
gt.xep.khoa: Lock the tower: no dragging or parameter edits until unlocked.
gt.xep.xoa: Remove the tower from the plot. A locked tower must be unlocked first.
gt.xep.nhom: Choose the tower group: commercial or social housing.
gt.xep.dat: Place this tower template at the centre of the lot's building line.
gt.tang.kieu: Floor-plan drawing style (colour by unit type, technical lines...).
gt.tang.hienTem: Show the name and clear-area label on each unit.
gt.tang.noiThat: Draw sample furniture inside the units.
gt.tang.chamMau: Colour dot beside each unit's clear area against the business brief: green if within the threshold, red if beyond. The area threshold is provisional, awaiting the lead's decision.
gt.tang.suaNhieu: When swapping a unit's template, swap every unit of the same template in the tower.
gt.tang.toiUu: Automatically swaps templates with the same width, depth and middle/corner position to bring the mix closest to the target. Units are never redrawn.
gt.tang.veGoc: Reset every unit of the tower to the tower template's original units.
gt.sc.dtLo: Plot area computed from the boundary on the drawing.
gt.sc.dtxdMax: Maximum footprint = plot area x maximum coverage.
gt.sc.dtxdThapMax: Maximum tower footprint = plot area x maximum tower coverage.
gt.sc.dtSanMax: Maximum floor area = plot area x maximum FAR (QCVN 01:2021/BXD, 1.4.21).
gt.sc.soCan: Unit count from the planning table, or estimated as maximum population / persons per unit when the table gives none.
gt.sc.choDo: Car spaces required = units x minimum car spaces per unit.
gt.sc.choXeMay: Motorbike spaces required = units x minimum motorbike spaces per unit.
gt.sc.cayXanh: Green area required = plot area x minimum green share.
gt.dong.matDo: Achieved coverage = footprint / plot area, against the maximum.
gt.dong.matDoThap: Achieved tower coverage against the planning maximum.
gt.dong.dtSan: Floor area counted in the FAR (using the current floor-area factors), against the maximum (QCVN 01:2021/BXD, 1.4.21).
gt.dong.tangCao: Storeys of the tallest tower, basements excluded, against the maximum.
gt.dong.tangDe: Podium storeys of the scheme against the planning figure.
gt.dong.tangCanHo: Apartment (tower) storeys of the scheme against the planning figure.
gt.dong.soCan: Total units of the scheme against the planning table.
gt.dong.danSo: Population of the scheme = units x persons per unit (provisional), against the maximum.
gt.dong.choDo: Car spaces provided against the number required (QCVN 04:2021/BXD, 2.2.17.1).
gt.dong.cayXanh: Green area provided against the planning minimum.
gt.ps.chon: Pick a saved preset to apply it at once to the plot / scheme.
gt.ps.phamGiaiThich: Selected plot: only changes this plot's planning indicators and target mix. Whole scheme: changes every high-rise housing plot plus the scheme's floor-area factors, colour thresholds and basement parameters.
gt.ps.luu: Save the current settings as a named preset (same name overwrites). Stored in this browser.
gt.ps.xuat: Export this group's presets to a JSON file to share
gt.ps.nhap: Import presets from a JSON file (same name overwrites)
gt.ps.giaiThichCap: Level preset: a named bundle of planning indicators, target unit mix, floor-area factors, colour thresholds and basement parameters. E.g. "Commercial Hanoi", "Social housing".
gt.ps.giaiThichMuc: Section preset: saves and loads only the fields of this section.
gt.ps.khongLuuDuoc: Cannot save (no plot yet, or the browser blocks storage).
gt.ps.loiNhap.hong: The file is not a Unitmix preset.
gt.ps.loiNhap.sai_nhom: This file belongs to a different preset group.
gt.ps.loiNhap.rong: The file has no valid presets.
gt.ps.loiNhap.kho: Could not write to browser storage.
